authorRole: WP-16 part 1 spec author (forbidden from later implementing WP-05/WP-17/WP-18)
law: plan: Bounded successor complexity — 'EK-1 must freeze a machine-readable, conjunctive complexity envelope before EK-2 changes production code. A single weighted score, line-count target or prose claim is not an envelope: every dimension must pass independently.'
plan: Bounded successor complexity — 'A legacy baseline is diagnostic evidence, not an entitlement for the new kernel to be equally complex.'

plan: Bounded successor complexity — 'A newly discovered incident may add a minimized scenario. It may not add a state, relation, mutable owner, orchestration path or policy layer until an independent verifier approves a measured complexity delta before code is written.'
plan: Bounded successor complexity — 'EK-13 permits no active complexity waiver and no unmeasured dimension.'

determinismContract.requirement: plan EK-1: 'Run deterministic measurements twice on the same tree and require the same complexity vector' — byte-identical output, no clock, no randomness, sorted iteration, canonical JSON
determinismContract.proofCommand: node docs/refactoring/event-kernel/specs/measure-complexity.mjs --out run1.json && node docs/refactoring/event-kernel/specs/measure-complexity.mjs --out run2.json && cmp run1.json run2.json

conjunctiveEvaluation: Every dimension passes independently (AND over all dimensions). target.kind: 'max' (measured <= value), 'exact' (measured === value), 'closed-set' (measured set equals value exactly), 'subset-of-frozen' (measured is a subset of the frozen allowed set), 'zero-after-phase' (measured === 0 once the named phase has landed). The predecessor baseline NEVER satisfies a successor target implicitly: on the predecessor tree the vector is diagnostic; on a tree containing src/workflow-kernel the targets are binding and measure-complexity.mjs --check exits nonzero on any violation or unmeasured dimension.

waivers.policy: No waiver mechanism exists. Any change to any target reopens EK-1 per the plan and requires an independent-verifier-approved measured complexity delta BEFORE code is written.

deltaPolicy.addDimension: Forbidden after freeze unless an independent verifier approves a measured complexity delta before code is written (plan EK-1). A newly discovered incident may add a minimized scenario, never a state, relation, mutable owner, orchestration path or policy layer.
deltaPolicy.widenTarget: Reopens EK-1; invalidates downstream qualification evidence (plan EK-1 admission-specs).
deltaPolicy.shrinkTarget: Permitted (tightening) without reopening EK-1, but must be recorded as a new budget revision with rationale and digest.

dimensions.rationale: Alternatives are conditional parsing, and conditional parsing is where 'which authority did you mean' hides. The mutation corpus must prove an added alternative is red.

dimensions.title: Contract shape — maximum reference fan-out (refs per array and reference-valued fields per record)
dimensions.planMandate: plan: Bounded successor complexity — contract-shape dimension 'reference fan-out'

baseline.unit: no admission schemas exist on the predecessor tree (target-only dimension)
baseline.citation: predecessor analogue for scale: the material family touches 29 tables from one chain (census §4) — unbounded fan-out is the documented failure shape

target.detail: every reference array in the admission schemas carries maxItems <= 16 (allowedCapabilityRefs, allowedToolRefs, inputProductContracts, outputProductContracts, evidenceObligations) and each record holds at most 16 reference-valued fields

dimensions.rationale: Fan-out is combinatorial review cost: 16 refs per array keeps every contract reviewable while exceeding any legitimate 2-role x 4-profile need.

dimensions.title: Contract shape — maximum schema nesting depth
dimensions.planMandate: plan: Bounded successor complexity — contract-shape dimension 'maximum depth'

baseline.unit: no admission schemas exist on the predecessor tree (target-only dimension)
baseline.citation: predecessor contrast: buildPrompt composes ~12 unbounded layers with no schema at all (census §7.2 PA-1)

target.detail: admission schemas nest at most 3 levels deep (record -> field group -> ref/digest pair); anything deeper is policy hiding inside structure

dimensions.rationale: Depth is where inline transition policy smuggles itself past review (plan: 'no... inline transition policy'); three levels cover contract -> refs -> digests and nothing else.

dimensions.title: Contract shape — policy-reference kinds (closed universe of reference suffixes)
dimensions.planMandate: plan: Bounded successor complexity — contract-shape dimension 'policy-reference kinds'; plan: Canonical role contract — 'The role contract binds content-addressed references'

baseline.unit: no admission schemas exist on the predecessor tree (target-only dimension)
baseline.citation: the closed set is frozen NOW by this budget from the plan's two contract blocks

target.detail: exactly these 10 reference kinds across the two admission schemas; adding a reference kind reopens EK-1 (plan: 'Adding a field or reference kind reopens EK-1')

dimensions.rationale: A closed reference universe makes every indirection auditable: ten kinds, each naming an installed content-addressed authority; an eleventh kind is a new authority channel.

dimensions.title: Contract shape — arbitrary metadata/extension fields
dimensions.planMandate: plan: Bounded successor complexity — contract-shape dimension 'arbitrary metadata/extension fields'; plan: Canonical role contract — 'contains no free-form metadata, extension bag, inline transition policy or executable policy blob'

baseline.unit: no admission schemas exist on the predecessor tree (target-only dimension)
baseline.citation: predecessor contrast: episodic task memory materializes attempt_count/previous_failures onto the mutable card (census §7.2 PA-6) — the metadata-bag failure mode

target.detail: zero fields matching metadata/extension/extra/custom/x-* and additionalProperties is false (or a closed object) everywhere in the admission schemas

dimensions.rationale: A metadata bag is an unmeasured dimension by construction: anything can hide in it. Zero is the only safe cap.

dimensions.title: Execution structure — phase count (exact)
dimensions.planMandate: plan: Bounded successor complexity — 'The execution structure is capped at the 14 named phases EK-0 through EK-13'

baseline.unit: phases declared in the plan document
baseline.citation: EK-0 through EK-13

target.detail: the plan may not grow a 15th phase; re-scoping merges or replaces an existing phase and reopens the admission decision

dimensions.rationale: Phase count is schedule-shaped complexity: hidden phases are untracked authority. The measurement reads the governing plan document itself, so adding a phase turns the checker red.

dimensions.title: Execution structure — top-level work-package count (exact)
dimensions.planMandate: plan: Bounded successor complexity — 'and the 24 top-level work packages listed below. A coordinator may split a package into tracked subtasks under the same owner/dependencies, but may not add another top-level package after EK-1 without replacing or merging an existing package and reopening the admission decision'

baseline.unit: top-level packages in the plan's work-package table

target.detail: tracked subtasks under an existing owner are legal; a 25th top-level package is a structural complexity delta requiring package replacement/merge plus reopened admission

dimensions.rationale: Work packages are ownership boundaries; adding one without removing another is authority sprawl. The measurement parses the plan table, so the cap is enforced against the actual document.
